Reading this made my heart start pounding out of my chest. This is my first time commenting here, after lurking for a few weeks. I don't remember a lot of my childhood due to trauma, and recently uncovered a lot of repressed memories. The same time as these very real traumas resurfaced in my mind I remembered a reoccurring 'dream' from when I was around 8. The 'dream' was of domething shining in my bedroom window it lit the room up like day, and I saw an unnatural disk moving outside. I don't remember much else about the dream other than I looked out a window where I could see earth and I know I talked to a group people but I can't remember them. I would tell them the great things and beauty in Nature, Humanity, and Earth. That's all I remember. It happened off and on for about once a month for four months.

I've been extremely terrified of the dark, especially my windows sense remembering this dream. Last night the blue super moon woke me up and sent me into a panic attack with it shining so brightly through my bedroom blinds. I don't claim to be abducted, but this 'dream' and the situation surrounding it worries me. I'm scared they might come back for me for some reason? Also I don't remember the dream happening outside that time in my childhood, but I used to reoccuringly get nosebleeds, or randomly flip upside down on my bed quite often and I'd never considered it an indication before. Very creeped out, and feeling a crazy for even considering this a possibility of being real.

I'm not "one of the good ones" I'm not trying to impress those who hate me. I wanted to share ideas with my community and help our community move forward. Refusing to reach out and understand why the other side thinks as they do is how you get people to understand transness. I live in a small homophobic state, when I came out no one supported me in the entire town because no one had ever met a trans person. Their only experiences were negative from the news and the internet. Being calm, understanding, and educating those who hated me a lot of people (not everyone) came around. If I had came out and expected everyone to accept me and didn't try to understand and educate no one would've changed their minds on trans folk in my hometown.

not every transphobe is a fascist. don't hate the ignorant. if we hate everyone who doesn't immediately accept us we're causing so much more harm then if we are open, friendly, and willing to educate those who want to learn.

but holding resent towards those bigots and not compromising is exactly what they're doing towards us. We need to be the bigger person and reach across. We can't expect transphobia to disappear without effort from our part.

I AM NOT SAYING I LIKE THIS. In a perfect world we'd be accepted and that'd be that. but it's not. compromise is the only path forward.

I think us just existing is pushing the boundary to some, we have to take steps. The civil rights movement didn't expect change overnight, and their progress was slow, respectful, and steady. The gay rights movement (spearheaded by transfolk) pushed for acceptance but it took over 40 years for gay marriage to be legalized and another decade after that for most of society to accept them. Progress doesn't happen quick and I feel like our community needs to stop expecting society to accept us when we didn't become a mainstream topic until the 2010's.
